audit.why: 7/10 with Aurora owning Levels 4-5 and 2+ items is right for the shape of the kits: a 900-range Twofold Hex and an 825-range The Weirding against a 300-range Chomp means she picks every trade until you have terrain and bulk, and Subjugate pays badly against a squishy mage.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every power window was pinned on 'Twofold Hunt (Blink)', an ability that does not exist, and the slot letters were wrong on top of that — spikes and whys call the blink 'E' and treat 'W spirit-exile' as a separate ability.
audit.why: Aurora's kit is Spirit Abjuration (P), Twofold Hex (Q, 9/8.5/8/7.5/7), Across the Veil (W, 22/21/20/19/18), The Weirding (E, 15/14/13/12/11) and Between Worlds (R, 140/120/100). The leap and the invisibility are one ability, Across the Veil, on W — not an E blink plus a separate spirit form.
audit.corrected: Rebuilt every spike and why on the real names and the real 22s / 15s / 140s cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four errors. (a) 'Twofold Hunt (Blink)' is fabricated and used ~23 times. (b) Chomp is said twice to slow her ATTACK SPEED — it saps Attack Damage and slows movement. (c) breakdown/mid claims she can 'stand inside your Frozen Domain, take zero damage in spirit form' — Across the Veil grants invisibility, not damage immunity or untargetability, so autos and ground zones still work where she landed. (d) 'Q root' — Twofold Hex does not root; the only slow in her kit is The Weirding, plus the Between Worlds zone.
audit.why: Riot Data Dragon. Across the Veil: 'leaps in a direction of her choosing, entering the spirit realm upon landing, becoming invisible, and gaining Move Speed'. Twofold Hex: 'sends out a missile that curses any enemies it hits... recast to draw active curses back toward herself' — no root. Chomp: 'dealing damage, briefly slowing and sapping some of their Attack Damage.' The interaction that actually decides the lane is Pillar of Ice being impassable terrain against a leap: place it on the far side of the leap, not on her body.
audit.corrected: Real names everywhere, Chomp corrected to AD sap, the invisibility-is-not-invulnerability point stated outright, and Pillar re-taught as a landing-spot denial against a 22s leap.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers anywhere despite the entire page being about tracking one escape.
audit.why: Across the Veil is 22s at rank 1 — the longest escape cooldown in her kit and a very large window; The Weirding is 15s and Between Worlds 140s.
audit.corrected: 22s / 15s / 140s now stated in the cooldown block, the report and the whys.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spirit Abjuration is never mentioned even though it is a continuous heal off every spell and auto she lands.
audit.why: Riot's passive text: 'Aurora's spells and attacks exorcise spirits from the enemies she damages. Exorcised spirits follow Aurora around and heal her.' The interaction file flags this matchup as anti-heal relevant.
audit.corrected: Named the passive as the reason her poke war is sustainable, without inventing an item timing.

edits.before: At level 1, Chomp your very first auto — the AD steal and attack-speed slow hit before she can do anything, and any minion dying nearby tops you back up through King's Tribute. She is weak here: no blink, no real escape, just a Q poke that costs mana. Step up when her Q is on cooldown, auto-Chomp, and back off; you win this micro-trade. The moment she hits level 2 and gets her E blink the dynamic starts shifting, so take the free damage now and save Pillar for when she tries to extend her Q walk-up into a longer trade.
edits.after: At level 1, Chomp your very first auto — the AD sap and the slow hit before she can do anything, and any minion dying nearby tops you back up through King's Tribute. She is weak here: no leap, no real escape, just Twofold Hex poke that costs mana. Step up when her Q is on cooldown, auto-Chomp, and back off; you win this micro-trade. The moment she hits level 2 and gets Across the Veil the dynamic starts shifting, so take the free damage now and save Pillar for when she tries to extend her poke walk-up into a longer trade.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are her window — Q root into W spirit-exile lets her stand inside your Frozen Domain, take zero damage in spirit form, and re-emerge after you've already committed your Pillar cooldown. Do NOT blow Pillar reactively when you see W cast; wait for her to re-enter the physical plane and THEN drop the ice to cut off the E escape route. If you Pillar first and she ghosts through it in spirit form, you have no terrain left to stop her from blinking out. At 6 her R reposition makes Subjugate nearly worthless — she isn't tanky enough to make the resistance drain matter, and she'll blink out of range before the second cast. Treat R as a deterrent rather than a kill tool in this lane; instead look for Frozen Domain all-ins when her E and W are both on cooldown simultaneously.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are her window — Twofold Hex chips you from 900 range and Across the Veil leaps her out of your Frozen Domain before the zone earns anything. She turns invisible on that leap, not invulnerable, so keep swinging where she landed and her Spirit Abjuration heal never gets to run away with the poke war. Do NOT blow Pillar the moment you see the leap start; it is impassable terrain, so put it beyond where she is going and the 22-second escape lands into a wall. Throw it early and you have no terrain left. At 6, Between Worlds makes Subjugate a poor opener — she is not tanky, so the drain is small, and her zone teleports her out of the 650-range recast. Treat R as a deterrent and all-in when Across the Veil and The Weirding are both down.

edits.before: With Iceborn Gauntlet online you tank enough AP burst that the matchup flattens back into a skill contest — your Chomp slow chain keeps her in range longer even when she's trying to kite, and the Gauntlet zone punishes her for standing still to cast Q. In teamfights your Subjugate absolutely shreds a tanky frontliner while Aurora splits her attention between peeling and dealing; that's where you reclaim value the lane denied you. Never hard-chase her in an open lane in the late game — her Q root and R can turn that into a free peel for her whole team. Force fights in the river or around objectives where your Pillar can wall off the chokepoint and her blink options are fewer.
edits.after: With Iceborn Gauntlet online you tank enough AP burst that the matchup flattens back into a skill contest — your Chomp slow chain keeps her in range longer even when she's trying to kite, and the Gauntlet zone punishes her for standing still to cast Q. Never hard-chase her in an open lane in the late game — The Weirding's slow and Between Worlds turn that into free peel for her whole team. Force fights in the river or around objectives where your Pillar walls the chokepoint and her leap has nowhere to go.

notes: 'Twofold Hunt (Blink)' is a fabricated ability name and appeared ~23 times across the full layer; replaced with Across the Veil (W). The content layer also had the slots wrong — it called the leap 'E blink' and treated 'W spirit-exile' as a separate ability, when Across the Veil is one W that leaps and grants invisibility. Killed the false claim that she takes 'zero damage in spirit form': Riot's text says invisible, not untargetable or invulnerable. Killed 'Q root' (Twofold Hex does not root) and the 'attack-speed slow' description of Chomp (it saps Attack Damage). Same 'attack speed' error appears in other Trundle matchups — worth a champion-wide sweep.
